faq.q: Will the text in my PDF still be selectable after compressing?
faq.a: No. This tool rasterises every page into a JPEG and rebuilds the PDF, so the output is images — text is no longer selectable, searchable or copyable, and you can't run text extraction on it. Compression is one-way and can't be reversed here, so always keep your original file. This trade-off is what allows the large 30–90% size reductions.

faq.q: Can it hit a specific size limit like 2 MB or 500 KB?
faq.a: Yes. Switch Mode to "Target size (auto-find quality)" and enter a KB target; it binary-searches JPEG quality over up to 7 attempts to land just under your limit. Presets set this up for you: Email (under ~5 MB), Government portal (under 2 MB), and Government portal strict (under 500 KB, grayscale on). If it can't reach the target even at lowest quality, it tells you to lower DPI or enable grayscale.

faq.q: What settings control the output size and quality?
faq.a: A fixed quality level (Maximum ~70–90% smaller, Medium, Light, Minimal), DPI (72, 100, 150 recommended, or 200 for print), optional grayscale conversion, and optional downscaling of large pages to a max width in pixels. You can also compress only a page range like 1-3,5. A live estimate probes the first two pages to predict the output size before you commit.

faq.q: Can I compress several PDFs at once?
faq.a: Yes. Drop multiple PDFs and they're queued for batch compression with the same settings. Each shows original vs compressed size, percent saved, and a before/after thumbnail of page 1 so you can check if the text got too soft. You can download each file individually or all of them together as a ZIP. A copyable compression report summarises every result. All processing stays in your browser.
